newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium checking reports of East Zaire "genocide".
newsitem.headline: Belgium checking reports of East Zaire "genocide".

text.p: Belgium is checking reports of mass killings in rebel-held Eastern Zaire, a foreign ministry spokesman said on Wednesday.
"We...have received the reports, particularly one from a witness in the area," the spokesman said. "We have contacted our ambassadors in the region to try to assemble and corroborate the reports."

Belgian Development and Cooperation Minister Reginald Moreels told Het Laatste Nieuws newspaper at the weekend he had received eyewitness reports that a new "genocide" was under way in East Zaire and that mass graves had been found.
"We are very concerned about human rights violations in territory to the East of Kivu," the foreign ministry spokesman said. He declined to talk in terms of genocide.
Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila held talks on Tuesday with South African officials who hope to broker a ceasefire in the central African country.
Kabila's forces have met little apparent resistance from President Mobutu Sese Seko's ill-disciplined and often unpaid army as they move westwards from their strongholds of Goma and Bukavu.
The rebels, who want to topple Mobutu, say they are only 30 km (18 miles) from the important eastern town of Kindu, where aid workers said residents were in panic.

The conflict, which escalated this month with the bombing of rebel-held towns, has sent tens of thousands of refugees fleeing and threatens to destabilise vast Zaire and its central African neighbours.
Belgian Foreign Minister Eric Derycke told parliament on Tuesday he believed Kabila was prepared in principle to accept the presence of international observers in captured territory.
Christian Tavernier, a Belgian who leads mercenaries fighting for the Zairian government, said on Sunday that rebel forces currently held the upper hand.
He also accused Uganda of supporting the rebels.
"There are well-organised armed units coming from Uganda who carry out an operation, attack a position, and then retreat," Tavernier told Belgian radio RTBF.
"That means...the balance of strength is currently against us," he said on the telephone from eastern Zaire.
He added: "The Zairean army is in a tangle, like the rest of the country, with almost no logistics."
